text:
tara: Quick postmortem follow-up for the embedding-service incident (2026-03-17), recurring tail latency / p99 burns. Need concrete owners and an interim SLO plan before next customer sync.

noah: Recap: p99 jumped due to a combination of oversized batches and fallback to slow CPU inference in zone C. It lasted ~9h with 2 smaller recurrences in the next 48h. Error budget impact ~2.7% this sprint.

frank: Noted. Two angles: 1) immediate mitigations (throttle large batches, raise batch timeout) 2) medium-term (shard-hotspot fix and better cross-zone routing).

noah: Proposal for immediate SLO guardrails: set an adaptive p99 target window (last 7d) and enable temporary backpressure on non-critical batch jobs when p99 > 1.5s for 30m.

sre-bot: Automated suggestion from runbook engine: consider adding a "SLO Safeguard" feature flag that drops non-urgent batches to priority queue.

tara: I like the feature-flag approach. Owner suggestions: - immediate backpressure & flag rollout: noah - shard-hotspot investigation: frank - dashboard + SLO window update: ops

ops: I'll add a new dashboard tile: "p99 recurrence rate" (counts of p99 breaches per 24h) and a heatmap by zone. ETA 2026-03-25. Will also add an alert.

ops: Alert draft:
```
alert: EmbeddingServiceP99Recurrence
expr: increase(embedding_request_latency_p99[24h]) > 0.2
for: 1h
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/runbooks/embedding-p99.md
  summary: "Embedding service p99 recurrence above threshold"
```
This triggers only on sustained recurrence.

noah: For the immediate backpressure I'll open a small PR gating large-batch submissions and a flag to drop low-priority work in 2 hours. Plan: canary in eu-west first, then us-east.

frank: For hotspots I will run a cross-zone trace sweep to find shard imbalance and post results by 2026-03-22. If we need re-sharding it's a longer task (4-6 weeks).

tara: SLO conversation: don't change permanent SLOs yet. Short-term: create an "operational window" annotation on dashboards explaining how we handle p99 recurrence (backpressure, canary). If after the medium-term fixes we still see >2% monthly burn, escalate to product for SLA customer comms.

noah: Actions and owners (please ack):
- immediate backpressure flag + small PR: noah, ETA 2026-03-19
- dashboard tile + recurrence alert: ops, ETA 2026-03-25
- shard imbalance trace & report: frank, ETA 2026-03-22
- runbook update with regression playbook: ops, ETA 2026-03-21
- postmortem action tracker update + customer impact note: tara, ETA 2026-03-20

frank: ack 1:10. I'll include measured shard distributions and synthetic repro steps.

noah: ack 1:12. PR created: https://git.redwood.ai/services/embedding/pulls/128 (will link canary rollout).

ops: ack 1:15. Dashboard PR: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/dashboards/pulls/61

tara: ack. I'll post weekly status summaries here and ping product on 2026-03-26 if burn >2% persists.

noah: One more ask 1: can we add a label to incidents that are "recurrence-prone" so runbook engine surfaces related fixes? makes triage faster.

ops: good idea. I'll add the label taxonomy to our incident template.

tara: Thanks all. Short cadence here: weekly updates in this thread, escalate if any owner misses ETA.

sre-bot: New canary rollout scheduled by noah for 3952109000. Notifying oncall schedule.
